answer.answer: U.S. export controls have left NVIDIA unable to create and deliver a competitive data center product for China that is approved by both the U.S. and Chinese governments, and as of the end of fiscal year 2026 it was effectively foreclosed from China's data center compute market [1]. The controls cover multiple chip parameters, including total processing performance, performance density, interconnect bandwidth and memory bandwidth [1]. Any H200 shipped to China under the new licensing program must go through a U.S. inspection process and would be subject to a 25% tariff on import into the U.S., which NVIDIA may not be able to pass along to customers [1]. The controls have also hurt NVIDIA beyond China, since they have negatively impacted demand in Europe, Latin America and Southeast Asia and led to excess inventory and purchase obligations with the H20 [2]. In addition, China's antitrust regulators preliminarily found that NVIDIA's compliance with U.S. export controls, which required it to offer degraded products to the Chinese market, violated the terms of China's approval of the Mellanox acquisition [3]. The Chinese government has also encouraged customers to buy from China-based competitors and discouraged purchases of NVIDIA's data center products, including any China-specific product designed to comply with U.S. export controls [4].

answer.answer: On September 8, 2025, PTFI experienced an external mud rush incident at the Grasberg minerals district that resulted in seven fatalities [1]. Approximately 800,000 metric tons of wet material entered the Grasberg Block Cave underground mine from the former Grasberg open pit and traveled rapidly to multiple levels of the mine, including a service level where seven team members were later found deceased [2]. Mining operations were temporarily suspended to prioritize recovery of the seven team members and to conduct investigations [1]. In late October 2025, PTFI restarted operations at the unaffected Deep Mill Level Zone and Big Gossan underground mines, and a phased restart and ramp-up of the Grasberg Block Cave underground mine is anticipated to begin in second-quarter 2026 [2]. The company expects the incident to have a significant impact on its 2026 operating and financial results [2].

answer.answer: Duke Energy's Electric Utilities and Infrastructure segment serves customers across six states in the Southeast and Midwest [1]. Duke Energy Carolinas and Duke Energy Progress each operate in portions of North Carolina and South Carolina [2]. Duke Energy Florida operates in portions of Florida [2]. Duke Energy Ohio transmits and distributes electricity in portions of Ohio and Kentucky, and it generates and sells electricity in portions of Kentucky [3]. Duke Energy Indiana operates in portions of Indiana [4]. Together these cover North Carolina, South Carolina, Florida, Ohio, Kentucky and Indiana [2][4].
